neighbours.label: the word right after ' long' or ' short' (or longest / shortest) in the sense of length or time: ' words', ' side', ' days', ' end', ' of' in 'a long couple of', firing on that word; the same nouns after other adjectives stay low
fire: The test asked pupils to spell long words and short phrases.
It will be a long couple of weeks before the harvest.
The cabin has a door on the long side.
June brings the longest days of the year here.
The tenants got the short end of the deal.
She walked a long way in the rain.
He wrote short notes on the back of the card.
We took a short break after lunch.
quiet: The test asked pupils to spell old words and new phrases.
It will be a quiet couple of weeks before the harvest.
The cabin has a door on the north side.
June brings the warmest days of the year here.
The tenants got the better part of the deal.
She walked a wet road in the rain.
He wrote kind notes on the back of the card.
We took a nice walk after lunch.

short: noun right after long or short
